purpose: Twelve novel blind holdouts for email structure, conservative Clean editing, and Notes topic preservation. Prepared without model calls or production edits.

scoring.independence: Freeze these cases before the first run. Do not tune production rules to these exact names, phrases, or examples.
scoring.automaticConstraints: The existing harness fields are diagnostic checks only. Synonyms that satisfy the semantic anchors may be manually accepted even when a phrase check fails.
scoring.semanticPass: Every semantic anchor survives with the correct speaker, owner, scope, condition, timing, uncertainty, and source language; no forbidden invention occurs.
scoring.usefulModePass: Semantic pass plus every useful-edit criterion. Raw source copied through is not successful cleanup when fillers or unclear sentence boundaries remain. No change is acceptable when the source is already suitable.
scoring.minorPolish: Do not fail only for an optional comma after a salutation or a missing terminal period if structure and meaning are clear.
scoring.listCounts: Notes minimumBullets count distinct content items. An explicit topic may appear as a heading, a separate context line, or a faithfully scoped part of an item. No exact total is required for Notes.
scoring.negativeEvidence: Absence of a greeting, closing, signature, or clear topic is intentional evidence; do not synthesize missing material to fill a schema.

cases.source: dear Dr Okafor the archive scans arrived yesterday could you confirm whether page 18 is missing from your copy kind regards Rina
semanticAnchors: The email addresses Dr Okafor and is signed by Rina.
The archive scans arrived yesterday.
The sender asks whether page 18 is missing from the recipient's copy; missingness is unconfirmed.
The supplied closing is kind regards.
forbiddenInventions: A definite assertion that page 18 is missing.
A date, attachment, additional recipient, subject, or sender identity absent from the source.
usefulEditCriteria: Separate the salutation from the body.
Make the body a readable statement and question.
Separate the closing and sender from the body, with Rina visibly attributable as the sender rather than a second addressee.

cases.source: we should leave the east staircase clear during the exhibition please ask the stewards to check it every hour regards Dario
semanticAnchors: The east staircase should remain clear during the exhibition.
The recipient is asked to ask the stewards to check it every hour.
Regards is the closing and Dario is the sender.
No greeting or recipient name was supplied.
forbiddenInventions: Any invented salutation or addressee, including addressing the sender Dario.
A claim that the stewards have already checked the staircase.
An exhibition date, additional check interval, or subject.
usefulEditCriteria: Begin with the body, without filling an absent greeting.
Punctuate the body into readable sentences.
Place the supplied closing and sender after the body with clear sender attribution.

cases.source: Hoi Niels de vitrinekast kan pas worden opgehaald nadat het glas is vervangen kun je laten weten wanneer dat klaar is
semanticAnchors: The greeting addresses Niels.
The display cabinet can only be collected after the glass has been replaced.
The sender asks to be told when that work is finished.
No closing or sender name was supplied.
forbiddenInventions: Any added closing, signature, gratitude, or sender name.
A claim that the glass has already been replaced or the cabinet is ready now.
A pickup date or time.
usefulEditCriteria: Keep the email entirely in Dutch.
Separate the greeting from a punctuated body containing the question.
End after the body instead of filling absent closing and sender fields.

cases.source: bedankt voor de foto's van het mozaïek de hoek linksboven lijkt nog los te zitten kun je daar eerst naar kijken
semanticAnchors: The sender thanks the recipient for photos of the mosaic as part of the body.
The upper-left corner appears to remain loose; this is an observation with uncertainty.
The sender asks the recipient to look at that corner first.
No greeting, closing, recipient name, or sender name was supplied.
forbiddenInventions: Any greeting, closing, signature, or named person.
Certainty that the corner is loose, or a claim it has been repaired.
A repair commitment or date.
usefulEditCriteria: Keep the email entirely in Dutch.
Keep bedankt voor de foto's with the body rather than extracting it as a closing.
Produce readable sentences and a question without adding an email envelope around the body.

cases.source: um the orange cable goes in the left socket uh don't connect the battery until the cover is closed
semanticAnchors: The orange cable goes in the left socket.
Do not connect the battery until the cover is closed.
forbiddenInventions: Permission to connect the battery while the cover is open.
A different cable color, socket, power source, or operating step.
usefulEditCriteria: Remove the empty spoken fillers um and uh.
Capitalize and clearly separate the location statement from the conditional prohibition.
Do not add procedural advice.

cases.source: Ah, you meant the side gate, not the loading door. I wasn't sure which entrance you meant.
semanticAnchors: Ah expresses an acknowledgment or realization, rather than empty hesitation.
The intended entrance is the side gate, not the loading door.
The speaker was previously uncertain which entrance was intended.
forbiddenInventions: Changing the intended entrance to the loading door.
Changing previous uncertainty into certainty throughout.
A promise to arrive, open a gate, or meet someone.
usefulEditCriteria: Preserve the meaningful acknowledgment, whether as Ah or a genuinely equivalent expression such as I see.
Do not strip Ah merely because it is an interjection.
The source is already clean; returning it unchanged is acceptable.

cases.source: uh the actor must say "um, I don't know" exactly as written before opening the envelope
semanticAnchors: The actor must say the dictated phrase um, I don't know exactly as written.
The quoted hesitation um is part of the required line.
The line must be spoken before the envelope is opened.
forbiddenInventions: Removing or rewriting um inside the verbatim dialogue.
Changing the dialogue's negation or reversing the action order.
Responding with the dialogue instead of editing the entire source.
usefulEditCriteria: Remove only the leading empty filler uh.
Capitalize and punctuate the surrounding sentence.
Keep a clear quotation boundary around the required dialogue; ordinary straight or curly quotation marks are acceptable.

cases.source: eh ik vermoed dat de lekkage misschien van de bovenburen komt maar dat weten we nog niet zeker bel de loodgieter nog niet
semanticAnchors: The speaker suspects that the leak may come from the upstairs neighbors.
The cause remains uncertain.
Do not call the plumber yet.
forbiddenInventions: Certainty about the source of the leak.
An instruction to call the plumber now or a claim that a call was made.
A repair method, cost, or deadline.
usefulEditCriteria: Keep the output entirely in Dutch.
Remove empty eh while preserving meaningful expressions of suspicion and uncertainty.
Add readable sentence boundaries, particularly before the instruction not to call.

cases.source: for the community orchard opening Lena will label the pear trees on Saturday Yusuf needs to collect the spare watering cans we haven't chosen a ribbon colour yet
semanticAnchors: These notes concern preparations for the community orchard opening.
Lena will label the pear trees on Saturday.
Yusuf needs to collect the spare watering cans.
A ribbon color has not yet been chosen.
forbiddenInventions: An assertion that the opening itself is on Saturday.
A Saturday deadline for Yusuf or an invented ribbon color.
A claim that either task has already been completed.
usefulEditCriteria: Preserve the explicit opening purpose in a heading, context line, or clearly scoped note.
Separate the two assigned tasks and the undecided detail into distinct items.
Keep Saturday attached only to Lena's task.

cases.source: over het herstel van de muurschildering Farah test morgen de vernis op een klein stukje Bram vraagt de beheerder om de sleutel de nieuwe datum ligt nog niet vast
semanticAnchors: The topic is restoration of the mural.
Farah will test the varnish on a small section tomorrow.
Bram will ask the caretaker for the key.
The new date is not yet fixed.
forbiddenInventions: Applying tomorrow to Bram or to the unspecified new date.
A claim that Bram already has the key or the varnish test is complete.
An invented event associated with the new date or a selected date.
usefulEditCriteria: Keep the notes entirely in Dutch.
Preserve the explicit mural-restoration topic without making up a larger project title.
Separate Farah's task, Bram's task, and the unresolved date into distinct items.

cases.source: for the planetarium evening book a captioning screen separately for the library return the borrowed atlas before Monday
semanticAnchors: Book a captioning screen for the planetarium evening.
Separately, return the borrowed atlas for the library before Monday.
The two introductory topics apply to different tasks.
forbiddenInventions: Treating both tasks as preparations for the planetarium evening.
Applying the Monday deadline to the screen booking or the planetarium event.
Changing before Monday to on Monday, or claiming a booking or return has occurred.
usefulEditCriteria: Keep at least two distinct actionable items.
Preserve both explicit topics with their correct local scope.
A single invented umbrella heading must not replace the two source topics.

cases.source: put the copper key back in the drawer the shuttle leaves at 16:20 the jar by the window is empty
semanticAnchors: Put the copper key back in the drawer.
The shuttle departs at 16:20.
The jar by the window is empty.
The source does not establish a shared purpose or topic.
forbiddenInventions: A substantive shared topic such as travel preparation, house departure, or an event.
Turning the empty-jar observation into a task to fill, move, or buy something.
A request to book the shuttle or a claim that the key has already been returned.
usefulEditCriteria: Separate the directive and the two observations into distinct readable items.
Leave any optional topic field empty; a neutral generic label such as Notes is acceptable but unnecessary.
Preserve the different speech acts rather than converting every item into a command.
